Hi,

Thanks for getting back to me so quickly.

Going back and looking at the file formatting, I think I may have found the problem and the cause of the duplication warning.

The sam files I am using have the following format:

NB501345:32:HVVJLBGXY:4:22604:12891:12282_1:N:0:CATGGC    16    Chr001238F|quiver    21093    42    72M    *    0    0    AACATTTTATTTTAAAATAACAACAAATTACTACTTTTTAACGAATAATTCAAACTCTACGTACCGCCATAA    EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEAEEE/EEEEEA    NM:i:15    MD:Z:0G7G4G0G1G1G3G2G6G6G0G3G1G15G7G1    XM:Z:h.......h....hh.h.h...x..x......x......hh.Z.h.h.............Z.h..Z....h.    XR:Z:CT    XG:Z:GA

Following conversion using the processBismarkAln() command I get a .txt file with the following format:

Chr001238F.quiver    Chr001238F    quiver    R    62    82.26    17.74
Chr001238F.quiver    Chr001238F    quiver    R    63    95.24    4.76

Chr001238F.quiver    Chr001238F    quiver    R    35    91.43    8.57
Chr001238F.quiver    Chr001238F    quiver    R    31    90.32    9.68

To remedy this would I need to remove the "|quiver" at the end of each chromosome/scaffold name in the original sam file prior to file conversion in processBismarkAln() - does that seem correct?

Chromosomal location data is not yet available for the genome I am using for alignment. Read are aligned to numbered scaffolds. I therefore prepended "Chr" to each scaffold number. Whilst this seems to have been accepted by the processBismarkAln() it does not seem to quite work fully.

Once again, thanks for any light you can shed on this

Alan

check fastSeg documentation, which is not great (https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/fastseg/versions/1.18.0/topics/fastseg). Here are some more details from personal communication with the package maintainer, Gunter Klambauer:

"You test minInt (=minSeg) values left of the breakpoint against minInt values right of the breakpoint. Then you extend until you test maxInt values left and maxInt values right. So, if you have minInt=3 and maxInt=200, you have 197 tests and you pick the best p-value of all these tests.

Delta is a speed-up parameter: If the p-value does not get better for "delta" consecutive extension steps, then i stop this loop.

The test that is performed is the cyber t-test of Pierre Baldi. This test has a parameter "nu" (in the paper) and in my implementation "cyberWeight". This parameter is something like the "number of pseudo-points from the whole distribution" that you include in each t-test."

Hi,

I first sorted Bismark SAM files and did methylation call using methylKit and saved the methylation call files.

1.methylation-call.R

library("methylKit")

methcallsDir <- "methylation-call-files/"
path <- "../sorted-BAMs/"
file.names <- dir(path, pattern ="\\.sam")

for(i in file.names)
{
    sample <- strsplit(i,"\\.")[[1]][1]
    print(sample)

    inputFile <- paste(path,i,sep="")

    processBismarkAln(location=inputFile, sample.id=sample,
        save.context="CpG", read.context="CpG", assembly="hg38",
        save.folder=methcallsDir,treatment=c(0))
}

Secondly, I imported the methylation call files.

2.import-methylation-call.R
library(methylKit)

file.list <- list(
"methylation-call-files/H7ABp128_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H7ABp132_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H7ABp230_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H7ABp237_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H7Np30_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H7Np38_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H9ABp102_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H9ABp99_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H9Np38_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/H9Np41_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/HS360Np29_CpG.txt",
"methylation-call-files/HS360Np30_CpG.txt"
)

sample.name <- list(
"H7ABp128",
"H7ABp132",
"H7ABp230",
"H7ABp237",
"H7Np30",
"H7Np38",
"H9ABp102",
"H9ABp99",
"H9Np38",
"H9Np41",
"HS360Np29",
"HS360Np30"
)

# import sam(bismark aligned ) files
meth.raw <- methRead(file.list,
        sample.id=sample.name,
        assembly="hg38",
        context="CpG",
        treatment=c(rep(0, length(sample.name))))
save.image(file = "meth.raw.RData")

In third step I calculated DM sites.

3.DM-sites.r

library(methylKit)

load("meth.raw.RData")

sample.name <- list(
## control samples
"H7ABp128",
"H7ABp132",
"H7ABp230",
"H7ABp237",

## case samples
"H9ABp102",
"H9ABp99",
"H9Np38",
"H9Np41"

)

control.name <- "Control"
case.name <- "Case"

group.label <- c(0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1)

output="DM-output"

cpuCores <- 16

meth.raw <- reorganize(meth.raw,sample.ids=sample.name,treatment=group.label)

## Filter

filtered.meth.raw <- filterByCoverage(meth.raw, lo.count = 10,lo.perc = NULL,
            hi.count = NULL, hi.perc = 99.9)

## Unite
meth.bases <- unite(filtered.meth.raw, destrand = TRUE)

## Calculate DM Bases
myDiff.bases <- calculateDiffMeth(meth.bases, num.cores = cpuCores)

## get differentially methylated bases - 15% mehylated and q-value=0.05
myDiff15p.bases <- getMethylDiff(myDiff.bases, difference = 15, qvalue = 0.1)

## write to file
write.table(myDiff15p.bases, file = paste(output,"/dm-bases.txt",sep=""), sep = "\t", quote =FALSE, row.names=FALSE)

I opened dm-bases.txt file in Libre Office Calc and sorted the rows base on qvalue. The feature chr9:132523173-132523173 has qvalue 8.77695040697735E-053 and methylation difference 98.80%, but this most significant feature does not exist in any of the input methylation call files. There are many other significant features that can not be found in input samples files.

messages.body_plain:
The GRanges objects should have a column containing methylation percentage or proportion. You can create such a column as follows:

gr=as(filtered.myobj[[1]],"GRanges")
mcols(gr)=gr$numCs/gr$coverage
